title: Legal Profession Uniform Law (NSW)
summary: NSW applied the Legal Profession Uniform Law (enacted in Victoria) from 1 July 2015, creating a common legal services market with Victoria.

instruments.title: Legal Profession Uniform Law Application Act 2014 (NSW)
Legal Profession Uniform Law Application Regulation 2015

commenced.what: Uniform Law commenced in NSW and Victoria

direction_rationale: A single regulatory regime across participating states lets lawyers and firms practise across borders with one set of rules, reducing compliance costs and barriers to interstate expansion.
comparison: Non-participating jurisdictions (QLD, SA, TAS, ACT, NT); WA joined 2022
confounders: growth of legal tech and incorporated legal practices
notes: No separate CPI class for legal services.

verified.notes: NSW Application Act assent (20 May 2014) reported by the Law Society of NSW; left null.

assessment.summary: One set of rules for lawyers across participating states, so firms can practise across borders under a single regime. A modest gain for a national legal services market.

marks.reason: A common legal services market across participating states replaces separate regimes.
Firms working in several participating states comply with one set of rules.

assessment.confidence_note: The archived econometric evaluation found no detectable effect on legal services entry or exit (grade Moderate).
